title: Singing at the Casino Gardens in Robbins for Bill Bottoms; pianist Clyde Jenkins
summary: Clyde Jenkins, who heard her records, got her into Bottoms's show at the Casino Gardens; they discuss tracking Jenkins down.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Well, just to go back to this story now, we had some dates here. And, uh, did you get any, uh, work as a result of this recording date with Johnny Sincer? And when those records came out, did you, uh, happen to get a job as a result of it? You told me you went to work for Bill Bottoms about a year later.
Yes.
And had you worked, uh, in, uh, in the cafés before that?

No, I hadn't worked in, in the cafés before then. But, um, there was a fellow named, uh, uh, uh, uh. Wait a minute. I'll tell you in just a minute. He belongs to our club. Now, let's see. Uh, uh, uh, but anyway. Oh, my goodness. Why can't I think of that fellow's name? I'm so simple. I'm stupid. I just forget everything. Uh, uh, Clyde, uh, Clyde, Clyde Jenkins. Clyde Jenkins is his name, see. He heard me singing, and he heard the records. And he used to come to our house where we lived up there on, on, uh, Indiana. Uh, so, um, when Bottoms opened that place, he had the orchestra out there, out in, uh, Robbins, Illinois. It was called the Casino Gardens. And so he came for me to, to be in, to sing in the show.
I don't remember, uh, uh, uh, Jenkins as a musician. Clyde Jenkins. What was his instrument? He plays piano. He's still, uh, still active as a piano? He's still, he's still. I mean, he plays.
Yes, he still works someplace on, way out northwest. Oh, so. Yeah, he's still working.
Uh, do you remember anybody else who was with you at, uh, Casino? Uh, the orchestra? Yeah.
No, I don't remember who was in his orchestra. Now, I can't, I have full memory that way.
All right. I, but, but, uh, I, I can get in touch with him. He's probably in the directory of the cheer club.
Oh, yeah, I, I suppose so. He may be. I'll look him up and, and, uh, ask about that.
He should be. He belongs to the, to the cheer club. He's probably in the corner of the choir club.
I'll look up.
Now, this is 60, uh, 61, something. How many pieces did Clyde have at, uh, Garcett's Theater? I think he had, I think he had five.
That's the first thing. He has an address, but he doesn't have a telephone number.
Mm-hmm. All right, I'll wrap him a note. Tell him that I talked with you. And, and I wish he'd call me and see if he had, Langley.
Mm-hmm. 6440 Langley.
And, and, and he's still, uh, playing, is he?
Uh-huh.
Good. Now, uh, there were some vaudeville acts in which the name Jenkins appears. I wonder if he might have been with that. Somebody in Jenkins.
I really couldn't say. I couldn't say. Possibly so. I don't know.
